name: Kara Koyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu
summary: Two Turkmen tribal confederations, the “Black Sheep” and the “White Sheep”, that ruled eastern Anatolia, Iraq and western Iran after Timur; Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu was among the strongest rulers of his time before the Safavids took over.

location.value: The Aq Qoyunlu ruled parts of eastern Turkey from 1378 to 1508 and later held Armenia, Azerbaijan, much of Iran, Iraq and Oman; the Kara Koyunlu held present-day Azerbaijan, Armenia and parts of north-west Iran, eastern Turkey and north-east Iraq.
location.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

terrain.value: Highlands of eastern Anatolia and Azerbaijan, Mesopotamian plains and the Iranian plateau.

resources.value: Pasture for herds, silk and caravan trade.

population.value: There are about 9 million Turkmen today (6.1 million in Turkmenistan, 2022 census). The page gives no figure for the confederations' subjects.

urbanisation.value: Tabriz was the capital; Diyarbakır and Baghdad were major cities.

migration.value: Turkmen tribes moved seasonally with their herds.

economicBase.value: Traditional work was farming, cattle breeding and crafts, with semi-nomadic herding of sheep and camels. Taxes on the silk trade are not mentioned.

tradeRoutes.value: Silk routes from Iran to the Ottoman Empire and Europe through Tabriz.

wealth.value: Rich from trade under Uzun Hasan.

moneyAndTax.value: Silver tankas; Uzun Hasan’s tax code (the Qanun-nama).

inequality.value: Rulers and military elites above farmers and herders.

governmentType.value: Tribes united in military alliances; tribal relations lasted into the 1900s. Turkmen tribal representatives founded the Kara Koyunlu and Ak Koyunlu states. The page does not describe a sultan or khan from a ruling clan.

keyRulers.value: Kara Koyunlu: Qara Yusuf (took Tabriz and executed Shaykh Uways in 1410) and Jahan Shah (crowned 1438, died at Chapakchur in 1467). Aq Qoyunlu: Uzun Hasan (seized power 1452, reunified the state 1457, zenith) and Yaqub (1478–1490).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Contested between brothers and sons, often by war.

institutions.value: Tribal leaders and a Persian bureaucracy.

armyAndTech.value: Turkmen cavalry; few firearms, which cost them at Otlukbeli.

majorWars.value: Timur defeated the Qara Qoyunlu in 1400 and Qara Yusuf fled to Egypt; Uzun Hasan lost to the Ottomans at Otlukbeli but the dynasty survived.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: The Aq Qoyunlu defeated the Kara Koyunlu (1467) and took most of Iran.

alliancesRivals.value: Venice sent envoys to Uzun Hasan against the Ottomans.

scienceEducation.value: Persian scholarship at the Tabriz court.

openness.value: Open to trade and to Venetian diplomats.

religion.value: The Aq Qoyunlu are listed as Sunni, though Uzun Hasan kept ties to Shi’ism-leaning dervish orders. For the Kara Koyunlu, Minorsky wrote that they adopted Shia Islam as a unifying ideology while Bosworth disputed strong Shi’i sympathies among many Turkmen.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

socialStructure.value: Turkmen tribal elite over Persian townspeople and farmers.

dailyLife.value: Tents for nomads; bread and dairy.

riseSignals.value: Aq Qoyunlu: founded in the Diyarbakır region by Qara Yuluk Uthman Beg, ruling from 1378. Qara Qoyunlu: dated from about 1374 in the article and about 1375 in a cited Britannica line, so the start differs by a year.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: The Aq Qoyunlu reached their zenith under Uzun Hasan, who moved to a new capital at Tabriz (Tabriz 1468–1478, Âmid/Diyarbakır 1403–1468 in the infobox). He beat Jahan Shah of the Qara Qoyunlu at Chapakchur in 1467.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

outcome.value: Qara Qoyunlu ended 1467–1468 after Jahan Shah died at Chapakchur. Aq Qoyunlu: Ismail I’s Safavids beat them at Nakhchivan in 1501; the infobox gives summer 1503 for the collapse in Iran and 1508 for the end in Mesopotamia.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Aq Qoyunlu and Kara Koyunlu (checked 13 Nov 2026)

overallCertainty.value: Main events are known from chronicles; population figures are estimates.
